## Open

### T-742 — Test that the CLI serves the page

> _2026-11-20 · tools/blong-log · open_

`F-773`'s remaining half: nothing starts the CLI and asks for `/`. Add a test that runs
`node src/cli.ts --http-port <free> --udp-port <free>` as a child process, waits for `/health`, and
asserts that `/` answers 200 with the shell and that `/app.js` answers 200 — the failure this would
have caught was a `public/index.html` that did not exist, which no unit test can see because the
server answers 404 by design for a missing asset.

Keep it cheap: the child is killed in a teardown, the ports are fixed to the range the other server
tests use rather than chosen, and the assertions stop at the HTTP status and one marker in the body.
The bundle itself is a build artefact, so skip `/app.js` when `public/app.js` is absent rather than
failing a checkout that never ran `node build-client.js`.

### T-354 — The FilteredServer snapshot depends on stream timing

> _2026-10-16 · tools/blong-log · done_

The `LogViewer` `FilteredServer` story streams a log entry on a `setInterval` (up to 50 entries) and
`.storybook/test-runner.cjs` screenshots in `postVisit` without waiting for that stream to settle,
so the committed image snapshot depends on how many ticks fired before the shot: it passed in 771ms
on one run and failed at 0.527% differing pixels (4857 pixels) in 3310ms on the next. Freeze the
stream for the shot — stop the interval, or drive the count from a fixed seed — rather than widening
the snapshot threshold, which would hide a real render change.

FilteredServer streams ten bounded messages and the runner waits eight seconds before its shot; the
regenerated baseline shows the settled table and reproduced on a second run.

### T-743 — The viewer's package name does not resolve in this repository

> _2026-11-20 · tools/blong-log · done_

`log.destination.module` resolves from the working directory, which is what lets a deployment
install the viewer beside its process and name it as `@feasibleone/blong-log/writer`. In this
repository that name does not resolve: nothing depends on `tools/blong-log`, so the local rc has to
spell the file out (`./tools/blong-log/src/writer.ts`). That is documented, but it is the one thing
a reader gets wrong first.

Make the name work in the dev loop: either give a dev-facing package a `devDependency` on
`@feasibleone/blong-log` so the workspace link exists at the root, or have `blong-dev` learn a
`memory`-style token the rc can use. Decide which before changing the resolution rule, and keep the
path form working — a test's fixture module depends on it.

Obsolete: the sink is lukaot's and log.destination takes {host, port}, so no package name has to
resolve anywhere.

### T-744 — The viewer draws none of flow, decision, progress, intent or lineage

> _2026-11-20 · tools/blong-log · done_

The viewer now draws what else a record says: `RecordPanels.tsx` renders an intent, flow/leg,
status, parent and decision strip above an expanded row, a decision panel with the candidates in
evaluation order and the chosen one marked, and an exchange panel that reads both spellings
(`operation`/`target` with `status`/`elapsedMs`, and the pre-conversion `method`/`url` with
`statusCode`/`responseTime`). The accessors are `decisionOf`, `flowOf`, `intentOf`, `parentOf`,
`recordRefOf` and `exchangeOf` in `src/record.ts`, each with a case in `record.test.ts`, and a story
(`LukaotRecordContext`) plus its snapshot. The trace cell and the trace filter read `traceOf` rather
than `row.traceId`, so an entry handed straight to the viewer — a story, a fixture — shows its trace
too.

What remains, and why it is not done here: nothing in `realm/` produces a decision, a flow or an
intent, so the panels are only fed by fixtures. The next step is a producer — see the recommendation
recorded beside this: `blong-kustomize`'s reconcile run (a flow with plan/apply steps, granularity
and prune decisions, and an operator's intent) or `blong-agent`'s ticket run (a flow whose legs
cross into an engine and a model). Until one adopts them the chips stay empty in a real run.

Deliberately not built: server-side `flow`/`intent` query parameters. A chip filters by setting the
search text, which is client-side over the whole record, so it finds the run without a new round
trip; a `flowId` parameter belongs with the producer work, when there is something to ask for.

Viewer side complete and reviewed on sport records; intent now stated by the framework at the entry;
flow was already produced; first realm decision in sport's nomenclature merge.
